chunks: Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from Jaʿfar ibn Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad al-Hamadhānī, and he was with us as a pilgrim, who said:

I wrote to Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام by the hand of Abī: 'May I be your ransom, our companions have differed concerning the ṣāʿ. Some of them say that zakat al-fiṭrah is according to the Madanī ṣāʿ, while some of them say it is according to the ʿIrāqī ṣāʿ.'
So he عليه السلام wrote to me: 'The ṣāʿ is six riṭls by the Madanī measure and nine riṭls by the ʿIrāqī measure.'
He said: And he informed me, 'By weight, it comes to one thousand one hundred and seventy weight-units.'

key_terms.أَرْطَالٍ: riṭls, units of weight or measure
key_terms.الصَّاعِ: the standard volume measure used in zakat al-fiṭrah
key_terms.الْفِطْرَةُ: zakat al-fiṭrah, the alms due at the end of Ramadan
key_terms.بِالْوَزْنِ: by weight, as calculated in weight-units

ai.seo_question: What is the correct ṣāʿ measure for zakat al-fiṭrah according to Imam Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses a legal question about the correct measure of the ṣāʿ used for zakat al-fiṭrah. Imam Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام clarifies the equivalent values in both the Madanī and ʿIrāqī systems and also states its weight measure. The narration is significant for jurisprudential precision in fulfilling a religious financial obligation.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.2063 - It is narrated from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ja'far ibn Ibrahim ibn Muhammad Al-Hamadhani, who was with us during Hajj. He said:
"I wrote to Abu Al-Hasan (as) through Abu (a messenger), saying: 'May I be your ransom, our companions have differed regarding the measure of the sa': some say Zakat al-Fitr is based on the Madani sa', while others say it is based on the Iraqi sa'.'
Imam (as) wrote back to me: 'The sa' is six ritls (weights) by the Madani measure and nine ritls by the Iraqi measure.'
Imam (as) further informed me: 'By weight, it is 1,170 weights (units).'"
